title: Is Bhutan on to something with Gross National Happiness?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss Bhutan's concept of Gross National Happiness (GNH), adopted alongside its shift to a parliamentary democracy under King Jigme Singye Wangchuck. They cover the nine GNH domains, the 108-question survey and how indicators and thresholds are used for government accountability, and contrast Bhutan's approach with GDP-driven materialism in the US. They examine research on whether money buys happiness, including World Value Survey rankings (Denmark happiest), lottery winners versus amputees, the Princeton day-reconstruction study on income and mood, and the hedonic treadmill. They close with a recent Bhutan earthquake, listener mail about freerice.com, and an update on listener Ben's leukemia treatment.

segments.title: Opening banter and census worker news
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter, then discuss census takers and a census worker killing in Kentucky, leading into Bhutan's census.

segments.title: Bhutan's democratic transition and Gross National Happiness
segments.summary: The king of Bhutan abdicated in 2008 in favor of a parliamentary democracy, and the country adopted Gross National Happiness as a guiding principle alongside its new constitution.

segments.title: Nine domains and the GNH survey
segments.summary: Bhutan treats happiness as coming from within, surveyed households with a long questionnaire, and organized happiness into nine domains such as psychological well-being, community vitality, and ecology.

segments.title: Indicators, thresholds, and materialism in the US
segments.summary: Each domain is broken into indicators, with thresholds used to flag deficits for government action. The hosts contrast this with the US focus on GDP and materialism, and discuss the tension of Bhutan's poverty rate.

segments.title: Does money buy happiness?
segments.summary: The hosts review the World Value Survey, which ranked Denmark happiest in 2008 despite lower GDP per capita than the US, and criticisms of it. They also discuss lottery winners versus amputees and the hedonic treadmill.

segments.title: Income, mood studies, and money as a trap
segments.summary: A Princeton day-reconstruction study found income raises happiness up to a point, with little difference between the $50,000-89,000 and over $100,000 groups. The hosts discuss lifestyle inflation, divorce support, and the difficulty of taking a pay cut.

segments.title: Bhutan earthquake
segments.summary: Brief news segment on a magnitude 6.3 earthquake in Bhutan that killed at least twelve people and damaged ancient monasteries.

segments.title: Listener mail: freerice.com and Ben
segments.summary: A listener recommends freerice.com, where vocabulary answers donate rice. A listener named Ben, diagnosed with leukemia, is preparing for a transplant and has been listening to the show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts invite listener emails about leaving the rat race and close the episode with a sponsor line.
